posts.name: Nielzabub
posts.cooked: The easiest way to beat Iron Legacy is to shut down his damage. He primarily does Melee. He has a few cards that do other types of damage, psychic, toxic, and projectile, but more times than not he is going to be hitting you with Melee. Legacy is really good to take because a Next Evolution plus Lead from the Front can cancel all his damage, you can also have Visionary and Ra double team him with a Twist the Ether to turn all his damage into fire and have Ra Flesh of the Sun God to make everyone immune to fire. This is of course assuming you can get set up before he kills you.

Yep, I tackled IL today, and he's every bit as brutal as I'd heard…though if he hadn't lucked into opening on two damage reducers, I think we could have taken him or at least gotten close, what with him having only 32 HP.  But yeah, 3 damage to every hero target every round?  That's unheard-of.  And Demoralizing Presence is just a heinous card.  I plan to tackle the Freedom 6 game eventually; that's going to be just absurd.  4 damage to everyone and six Ongoings in play at the game start (with my luck one of them will be "Galvanized").

grim88:

in fact, I may have except Tempest was reducing damage fantatic was doing to herself, so she couldn't do her full 5 HP attack (Don't recall the name of the card)

That would probably be Sacrosanct Martyr.  (I was very sad when I noticed that this wasn't you dealing 5 separate instances of 1 damage to yourself, as I'd somehow thought.  That would be something else entirely.)

grim88:

I didn't want to use Legacy against him, thematically.

Actually Legs vs. Iron Legs is a totally on-theme match, since IL is an evil (or at least desperate and borderline-insane) future version of AFL, so AFL is literally facing the worst example of what he's capable of becoming.  Although the Scholar is also sort of fitting, just because he's The Dude who just wants to chillax and keep everything going smoothly, and IL is all about taking life super-seriously and being an insane control freak…they're precisely opposite personalities.  Scholar seems to be loafing around and wasting his life, but is actually adjusting the threads of destiny to ensure the ideal outcome with minimal effort; he's doing the right thing even though he looks nothing like anyone's idea of a hero.  IL on the other hand used to be THE super-hero, but now he's gone to ridiculous extremes in pursuit of an impossible ideal of a perfectly safe world, all because he refuses to admit that he could possibly be wrong.  The two might never meet - certainly Scholar probably wants to keep it that way - but they're totally made for each other.
